CAR-T QSP Model Validation

Layer 1 (numerical correctness) and Layer 2 (model sanity)

2026-06-07

1 Overview

This document works through a battery of validation checks for the corrected CAR-T QSP model. The goal is not to argue the model is right — it’s to rule out bugs so that downstream fitting against real data is interpretable.

Each check has an explicit pass criterion. If a check fails, the model (or the parameters, or the numerics) needs work before proceeding.

2 Model and baseline setup

Paste in the model exactly as in the main script, so this document is self-contained.

3 Layer 1: Numerical correctness

Each check here is asking the same question in different ways: is LSODA giving us the right answer, or is it giving us an artifact of step control?

3.1 1.1 Tolerance convergence

Solve at three tolerance levels. Trajectories should be indistinguishable at the 3-digit level between the middle and tight settings. If they disagree, either tighten further or reformulate — the model has numerical issues.

##    state rel_err_medium_vs_tight rel_err_loose_vs_tight
## 1      E                1.78e-06               1.83e-04
## 2 T_high                1.27e-05               1.24e-03
## 3  T_mid                8.07e-06               1.56e-03
## 4  T_low                2.94e-06               4.13e-05
## 5  sBCMA                6.24e-07               1.15e-04
## T_high range (medium): -6.251635e-10 6e+10
## T_high range (tight): -3.824662e-12 6e+10
## [1] 30709.6

Pass criterion: rel_err_medium_vs_tight should be < 1e-3 for all states. Loose will usually be worse, which is fine — it’s there to show the scale of the effect.

4 Diagnostic: find when and where the tolerance mismatch happens

## Max rel err at time: 29.5 d
##   T_high (medium): 1.242e-09
##   T_high (tight):  -1.051e-12
##   Absolute error:  1.243e-09

4.1 1.2 Method agreement

Solve with a completely different algorithm (dop853, an 8th-order explicit Runge-Kutta) and confirm agreement. Disagreement implies stiffness that one method handles and the other doesn’t, or a true algorithmic artifact.

##    state rel_err_lsoda_vs_dop
## 1      E             1.79e-06
## 2 T_high             1.42e-05
## 3  T_mid             8.92e-06
## 4  T_low             2.61e-06
## 5  sBCMA             5.29e-07

Pass criterion: relative error < 1e-3. If dop853 chokes entirely (fails to solve), the system is stiff and you’re right to prefer LSODA — but then tolerance convergence (1.1) is doing the heavy lifting for validation.

4.2 1.3 Constraint checks

Confirm states that must be physically valid never aren’t.

##                         check result
## 1 T_total never exceeds K_max   TRUE
## 2            E never negative   TRUE
## 3       T_high never negative   TRUE
## 4        T_mid never negative   TRUE
## 5        T_low never negative   TRUE
## 6        sBCMA never negative   TRUE
## 7 LD monotonically decreasing   TRUE

Pass criterion: all TRUE. The 1e-6 tolerance allows for tiny negative excursions at the level of atol (LSODA doesn’t enforce positivity). Larger negatives indicate either loose tolerances or a formulation problem.

4.3 1.4 Event handling

The bolus at t=0 should deliver exactly 0.75e8 into E. Check the jump.

##     time         E
## 1 -0.001         0
## 2  0.000  75000000
## 3  0.001  75126362
## 4  0.500 170954687
## 5  1.000 376400827

Pass criterion: E should be essentially 0.75e8 at t just after dosing, modulo fast dynamics. If you see a value wildly off, the dose compartment or event spec is wrong.

5 Layer 2: Model sanity

Each subsection below is a controlled experiment where the expected answer is known. If the model doesn’t produce it, something is structurally wrong and fitting against real data will produce nonsense estimates.

5.1 2.1 Zero-dose control: tumor grows logistically

No CAR-T infused. Tumor should grow toward K_max, effectors stay at 0, sBCMA tracks the tumor.

## Max |E| over 365 days: 0   (should be ~0)
## Final tumor / K_max: 0.9939569

Pass criterion: max(|E|) < 1e-6, tumor approaches (but doesn’t exceed) K_max. If tumor doesn’t grow meaningfully over a year at k_prolif = 0.02 with no killing, check that growth_factor isn’t capping too aggressively.

5.2 2.2 No-tumor control: effector decay

Set tumor compartments to 0, infuse CAR-T. With no antigen signal, expansion_drive collapses to just LD, and E should decay roughly exponentially at decay_rate. We can fit an exponential to the late-time trajectory and recover decay_rate.

## Expected effective decay rate: 0.1287 /day
## Fitted decay rate (t > 60):    0.1285 /day
## Ratio fitted/expected:          0.998

Pass criterion: fitted decay rate within ~20% of expected. Discrepancy is fine if LD hasn’t fully decayed by t=60 (it has — k_ld_recover = 0.08 gives half-life of ~8.7 days). Gross mismatch means the effector ODE isn’t what you think it is.

5.3 2.3 Antigen-density sweep: Hill function verification

Put all tumor in a single compartment and vary its antigen density. The initial kill rate at t=0⁺ (before expansion) should trace out the Hill function we specified. This directly checks the antigen pharmacology.

## Max rel error measured vs theoretical: 1.98

Pass criterion: points sit on the line (or very close — there’s some offset because E:T ratio isn’t quite saturated even at 1e12 dose). The shape must match: low at A=0, midpoint near EC50=50, plateau at high A.

5.4 2.4 E:T ratio sweep: new Hill function verification

Fix tumor and antigen, sweep effector dose across 4 orders of magnitude, look at initial kill rate. This traces out the new ET50 Hill we added.

## Max rel error measured vs theoretical: 1.98
## Normalized max error: 0.009

Pass criterion: measured sigmoid with midpoint at ET50 = 0.1 and plateau at Vmax_A. Confirms both Hill functions compose correctly.

5.5 2.5 sBCMA sink limiting case

As sBCMA → ∞, E_eff → 0, killing collapses to 0, tumor grows unimpeded. Force this by overriding initial sBCMA to a huge value.

## Day 365 tumor with huge sink:     3.14e+09
## Day 365 tumor baseline:           2.61e+04

Pass criterion: with huge sBCMA, tumor grows substantially more than in baseline. If it doesn’t, the sink mechanism isn’t working as intended.

5.6 2.6 Timescale plausibility

Check that CAR-T peak timing and magnitude fall in the clinically reported range: peak at day 7–21, peak magnitude ~10³–10⁵× the infusion dose (in cells/µL terms — but since our E has ambiguous units, we check relative to the bolus amount).

## Peak E at day:               28.5   (clinical: 7-21)
## Peak E magnitude:            1.58e+13
## Fold expansion vs bolus:     2.11e+05   (clinical: 10^3 - 10^5)
## Post-peak half-life (days):  14

Pass criterion: peak in the 7–21 day window, fold expansion in the 10³–10⁵ range, detectable contraction. If the peak is on day 2 or day 60, k_growth or the expansion_drive structure needs revisiting.

6 Summary

Layer Check What it rules out
1.1 Tolerance convergence Step-control artifacts
1.2 Method agreement Stiffness / algorithm-specific bugs
1.3 Constraint checks Physically impossible states
1.4 Event handling Dosing misspecification
2.1 Zero-dose control Background dynamics bugs
2.2 No-tumor control Effector ODE bugs
2.3 Antigen Hill sweep Antigen pharmacology structure
2.4 E:T Hill sweep New E:T saturation structure
2.5 sBCMA sink limit Shed-antigen mechanism
2.6 Timescale plausibility Gross parameter misspec

Once all checks pass, the forward simulator is trustworthy enough to build on — next steps are local/global sensitivity (Layer 3) and empirical validation against data (Layer 4).
